title: Real-Time Streaming with WebSockets & Server-Sent Events (PYTH_168_S1 to PYTH_168_S8)

slides.title: Full-Duplex WebSockets
slides.prompt: WebSockets enable persistent, bi-directional full-duplex communication between server and client.
slides.codeSnippet:
@app.websocket('/ws')
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()
    await websocket.send_text('Connected')

slides.title: Accepting WebSocket Connections
slides.prompt: Fill in the coroutine method called to handshake and establish a WebSocket session in FastAPI.

slides.title: Server-Sent Events (SSE) vs WebSockets
slides.prompt: When is Server-Sent Events (SSE) preferred over WebSockets?
options: When unidirectional server-to-client streaming (e.g., live stock feeds, logs) over standard HTTP is sufficient
When binary client file uploads are required
When low-latency peer-to-peer audio transmission is needed
When offline browser caching is required
slides.correctAnswer: When unidirectional server-to-client streaming (e.g., live stock feeds, logs) over standard HTTP is sufficient

slides.title: Receiving Async Messages
slides.prompt: Fill in the WebSocket method used to wait for incoming text messages asynchronously.

slides.title: Scaling WebSockets Horizontally
slides.prompt: How do you broadcast messages across multiple WebSocket server instances?
options: Using a Redis Pub/Sub backplane to relay events between server nodes
By keeping all client connections on a single server machine
By saving incoming messages in standard log files
By increasing browser HTTP timeout limits
slides.correctAnswer: Using a Redis Pub/Sub backplane to relay events between server nodes
